ego.name: Hans Erlwein
ego.summary: Hans Erlwein (1872–1914) was a German architect and municipal building official. He served as Stadtbaurat of Dresden from 1905 until his death, overseeing a large program of public construction and frequently integrating contemporary artists into municipal projects as unified works of architecture and art.

connections.relationship_description: Erlwein’s father, a hotelier in Bayerisch Gmain. Hans Erlwein’s full name was also Johann Jakob Erlwein, reflecting the shared family name.
Erlwein's mother; named in the biography as Johann Jakob Erlwein's wife Elise.
Erlwein's cousin (veter), an electrical engineer and electrochemist.

shared_activities: shared membership network in Corps Germania München
participation in corps-related social and alumni contexts
connections.notes: The specific intensity of direct personal contact is not stated in the provided text; the tie is evidenced through shared corps membership.

connections.relationship_description: Sculptor frequently integrated into Erlwein's municipal buildings in Dresden; cited as a younger visual artist Erlwein involved to create Gesamtkunstwerk-style civic architecture, including works at the Dresden slaughterhouse complex.

shared_activities: integrated architectural painting/decoration for the Italienisches Dörfchen (Dresden)
artist involvement in Erlwein-led municipal projects

category_summaries.summary: Erlwein’s personal life in the record is anchored by his parents (Johann Jakob and Elise), his wife Marie Hirsch (with whom he had a daughter), and his cousin Georg Erlwein.
His professional circle includes institutional commission contexts in Dresden, including projects connected to named legacy foundations (e.g., Krenkel and Meyer).
Erlwein repeatedly collaborated with contemporary artists to give municipal buildings a unified architectural and artistic character—especially Wrba, Gussmann, and Rößler.
Through Corps Germania München, Erlwein belonged to an elite associational network that extended beyond his formal municipal office.
